title: Build the OWA natively on Apple Silicon: Node 22.20.0, frontend-maven-plugin 1.15.4
body:
On an arm64 Mac, `mvn package` fails in `bedmanagement-owa`:

```
[INFO] Downloading https://nodejs.org/dist/v14.7.0/node-v14.7.0-darwin-arm64.tar.gz
[ERROR] Failed to execute goal com.github.eirslett:frontend-maven-plugin:1.6:install-node-and-yarn
        (install node and yarn) on project bedmanagement-owa: Could not download Node.js: Got error code 404
```

frontend-maven-plugin 1.6 maps `aarch64` to `darwin-arm64`, but Node 14.7.0 was never published for
darwin-arm64. Node only ships darwin-arm64 builds from v16 onwards. Until now, the only way to build was
`-Dskip.installnodenpm -Dskip.installyarn -Dskip.yarn -Dskip.npm`. That produces an omod whose
`bedmanagement.owa` has no `build/app.js` or `build/vendor.js`.

### Change (`owa/pom.xml` only)

- Node `v14.7.0` -> `v22.20.0`: the current LTS, and the version coreapps moved to in openmrs-module-coreapps#522.
  It is published for both darwin-arm64 and linux-x64.
- frontend-maven-plugin `1.6` -> `1.15.4`, the last 1.x release (requires Maven 3.6+). Since 1.12 the plugin fetches
  the native arm64 Node build for Node 16+ on Apple Silicon, instead of the x64 build under Rosetta.
- yarn stays at `v1.3.2`. `yarn.lock`, `package.json` and webpack 3 / babel 6 / jest 21 are unchanged.
  None of them is a native addon, and there is no node-sass.

### Verified

- macOS arm64, Java 21, scratch local repository: `mvn clean package` succeeds. The plugin downloads
  `node-v22.20.0-darwin-arm64.tar.gz`, and all 56 OWA jest tests pass.
- The omod's `web/module/owas/bedmanagement.owa` contains `build/app.js` and `build/vendor.js`.
- Node 16.20.2 and Node 22.20.0 produce byte-identical `app/build` output.
- The OWA also builds, and its tests pass, in a `linux/amd64` `node:22.20.0` container, which matches the ubuntu CI runner.

title: BED-40: Ending a visit with no bed assignment must not require bed write privileges
body:
**Ticket:** [BED-40](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/BED-40)

## Description

### Problem

Any user who may end visits but may not manage beds cannot end **any** visit while this
module is installed, including visits of patients who never had a bed. The REST call
(`POST /ws/rest/v1/visit/{uuid}` with a `stopDatetime`, which is what O3's "End active visit"
sends) answers `403` with "Privileges required: Assign Beds" (core's
`APIAuthenticationException: error.privilegesRequired`).

In an O3 RefApp 3.7.x distribution this hits every non-admin front-desk role: a records
officer or nurse can check a patient in and queue them, but cannot end the visit, unless
they are also given bed write access, which least-privilege rules out for an outpatient
front desk.

### Root cause

- `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/bedmanagement/aop/VisitWithBedPatientAssignmentSaveHandler.java:47-49`
  (identical at the 7.2.0 tag and on master): on every save of a persisted visit with a stop
  time, the handler calls `bedManagementService.unAssignBedsInEndedVisit(visit)`
  unconditionally.
- `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/bedmanagement/service/BedManagementService.java:121`:
  `unAssignBedsInEndedVisit` is
  `@Authorized(value = { "Assign Beds", "Edit Admission Locations" }, requireAll = true)`.
- Core's `AuthorizationAdvice` checks that annotation **before** the method body runs, so the
  check fires before `BedManagementServiceImpl.unAssignBedsInEndedVisit` (line 233) gets as far
  as looking up assignments, and fires even when the lookup would return nothing.

Stack trace from the new test before the fix:

```
org.openmrs.api.APIAuthenticationException: error.privilegesRequired
  at org.openmrs.aop.AuthorizationAdvice.throwUnauthorized(AuthorizationAdvice.java:133)
  at org.openmrs.aop.AuthorizationAdvice.before(AuthorizationAdvice.java:91)
  ...
  at jdk.proxy3/jdk.proxy3.$Proxy248.unAssignBedsInEndedVisit(Unknown Source)
  at org.openmrs.module.bedmanagement.aop.VisitWithBedPatientAssignmentSaveHandler.handle(VisitWithBedPatientAssignmentSaveHandler.java:49)
  at org.openmrs.aop.RequiredDataAdvice.recursivelyHandle(RequiredDataAdvice.java:291)
  ...
  at org.openmrs.api.impl.VisitServiceImpl.endVisit(VisitServiceImpl.java:194)
```

### Reproduction

1. A server with bedmanagement 7.2.0 (e.g. O3 RefApp 3.7.1).
2. A user whose roles grant `Edit Visits`, `Get Visits`, `Get Beds`, `Get Admission Locations`
   (and the usual read privileges for patients, visit types, locations), but **not**
   `Assign Beds` / `Edit Admission Locations`.
3. As that user, start a visit for a patient who has no bed, then end it (O3: Actions, End
   active visit; or `POST /ws/rest/v1/visit/{uuid}` with `{"stopDatetime": "..."}`).
4. Result: 403 "Privileges required: Assign Beds". Expected: the visit ends.

### Fix

The handler first asks `getBedPatientAssignmentByVisit(visit.getUuid(), false)` (the same
lookup `unAssignBedsInEndedVisit` itself performs) and calls `unAssignBedsInEndedVisit`
only if it returns an active assignment. Four lines in one file; no API or schema change.

Privileges:

- The new read requires `Get Beds` and `Get Admission Locations`. Saving any visit **already**
  requires both: `VisitWithBedPatientAssignmentValidator` calls
  `getBedPatientAssignmentByVisit(uuid, true)` on every visit save. So no user needs a new
  privilege.
- Ending a visit that **does** hold an active bed assignment still calls
  `unAssignBedsInEndedVisit` and still requires `Assign Beds` and `Edit Admission Locations`.
  The security of freeing a bed is unchanged.

### Tests

New, in `api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/bedmanagement/aop/`:

`VisitWithBedPatientAssignmentSaveHandlerUnitTest` (JUnit 5 + Mockito, same style as
`EncounterWithBedPatientAssignmentSaveHandlerUnitTest`):

| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handleShouldNotUnassignBedsWhenTheEndedVisitHasNoActiveBedAssignment` | FAIL (`NeverWantedButInvoked`: `unAssignBedsInEndedVisit` called

title: Upgrade to support OpenMRS Platform 3.0
body:
Updates bedmanagement so it builds against, and runs on, openmrs-core master (Platform 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT: Java 21, Jakarta EE, Spring 7, Hibernate 7). Same approach as the platform 3 upgrades of calculation (openmrs/openmrs-module-calculation#19), legacyui and webservices.rest.

## Changes
- Versions:
  - Module version is now 8.0.0-SNAPSHOT.
  - It builds against Platform 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT (with `openmrs-bom` imported), webservices.rest 5.0.0-SNAPSHOT and legacyui 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT.
  - `config.xml` now sets `require_version` to 3.0.0.
- Build:
  - Java 21 with `-parameters`.
  - The old source/target 8 settings, PowerMock exclusions and mockito-inline/byte-buddy pins are removed.
- Dependencies:
  - The api module no longer depends on `openmrs-web`, whose web test context broke every api context test.
  - The omod drops the javax servlet deps.
  - The omod also drops the unused `openmrs-atomfeed-omod` dependency, whose javax-based controller was picked up by REST's handler scan.
- `BedManagementDaoImpl`:
  - The Hibernate Criteria code is now HQL with the same filters, joins and paging.
  - `setInteger`/`setString` become `setParameter`.
  - Saves use `HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate`, and deletes use `remove`.
  - `retired=0` becomes `retired=false`.
- `BedTagMapDaoImpl` saves through `HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate`.
- `Bed.hbm.xml` uses `cascade="merge,persist"` in place of `save-update`, which is what core itself switched to.
- commons-lang becomes lang3.
- Tests:
  - Migrated to JUnit 5, and codehaus Jackson becomes Jackson 2.
  - Privilege test rows have the audit columns that core 3.0 requires.
  - `AdmissionLocationResourceTest`'s custom-representation key counts each go up by one, for the `resourceVersion` that REST 3.1+ adds.
- CI (release workflow and Bamboo) uses JDK 21.

## Verification
- `mvn clean install` passes: api 124 tests, atom-feed 5, omod 41.
- I deployed the omod on openmrs-core master (`mvn jetty:run`, MySQL 8) with legacyui, webservices.rest 5.0.0-SNAPSHOT, calculation, fhir2 6.0.0-SNAPSHOT, htmlwidgets, idgen, event, stockmanagement, serialization.xstream, metadatamapping, attachments, cohort and teleconsultation:
  - All modules started, and the server log has no errors from this module.
  - Logging in through the UI works.
- Over REST:
  - `bed`, `bedtype`, `bedTag`, `admissionLocation` and `beds?q=` respond.
  - Creating a bed type and a bed in a location works (201).
  - Beds list by location, and `admissionLocation/{uuid}` reports `totalBeds: 1`.

## Notes
- The atom-feed submodule still compiles against openmrs-atomfeed 2.6.3, which is javax/Hibernate 5 based. It only activates when the atomfeed module is installed, and that module is not part of the O3 distribution and hasn't been ported.
- The OWA's frontend plugin pins Node 14.7.0, which has no Apple Silicon build. That predates this change.

title: BED-39: prevent Hibernate premature flush
body:
I applied the fix to EncounterWithBedPatientAssignmentSaveHandler.handle and removed both calls to the @Transactional bed-management service that were forcing the premature flush:

- Void branch — instead of bedManagementService.deleteBedPatientAssignment(bpa, ...), the handler now sets the void flags directly on the attached bpa (setVoided/setDateVoided/setVoidReason/setVoidedBy), mirroring exactly what the soft-void method did. It uses the handler's user/date params for the void metadata.
- Start-datetime branch — dropped the explicit saveBedPatientAssignment(bpa); just mutating the attached entity is enough.

Both bpa instances come from a readOnly query so they're persistent and attached; their changes now flush with the surrounding transaction, after the unrelated VisitAttribute has had its valueReference populated — so the DataIntegrityViolationException no longer fires.

The bedManagementService field is retained because it's still used for the read-only getBedPatientAssignmentByEncounter lookup, which doesn't trigger a flush.

title: Prevent bed type from being nulled out on patient unassignment
body:
When unassigning a patient from a bed, the getBedByPatient query in BedManagementDaoImpl used a partial HQL projection selecting only bedNumber and id:
This returned a Bed object with all other fields — including bedType — as null. When the service subsequently called saveBed() on this incomplete object, Hibernate persisted the null bedType back to the database, wiping the bed's type configuration on every patient discharge.
The fix is to ensure that when one is unassigned bed, bed type configuration is maintained.
